blocks.content: Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation in the field of parliamentary procedures and has been in existence since 1962.

items: Zero Hour is NOT mentioned in the Rules of Procedure; it is an informal device available to members of Parliament.
Starred questions allow supplementary questions, whereas unstarred questions require written answers and do not allow supplementary questions.
Quorum for either House of Parliament is 1/10th of the total number of members under Article 100 of the Indian Constitution.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Zero Hour is an informal Indian parliamentary innovation starting immediately after the Question Hour.
Question Hour is the first hour of a parliamentary sitting dedicated to asking and answering questions.
Starred Questions require oral answers and permit supplementary questions to be asked.
Unstarred Questions require written answers and do not allow supplementary questions.
Guillotine Closure refers to putting remaining clauses of a bill or budget demands to vote directly without further discussion.
